Income Tax Folio S3-F2-C1: Capital Cost of Depreciable Property

1. Introduction

This folio discusses the capital cost of depreciable property for the purposes of claiming capital cost allowance (CCA).

The capital cost generally includes the purchase price of the property plus any costs incurred to acquire the property.

2. Determining Capital Cost

The capital cost of a property is determined at the time of acquisition. For most properties, this is straightforward.

2.1 Acquisition Costs

Costs that are included in capital cost:

  • Purchase price
  • Legal fees
  • Accounting fees
  • Installation costs

3. Passenger Vehicles

Special rules apply to passenger vehicles. The capital cost is limited to $30,000 (plus applicable taxes) for vehicles acquired after a certain date.

This limitation prevents taxpayers from claiming excessive CCA on luxury vehicles.

4. References

Income Tax Act: Subsection 13(7), definition of "capital cost"
